plan_a_advantages: More frequent and varied easy runs promoting aerobic base building.
Specific focus on running mechanics (rhythm, breathing, cadence) to improve efficiency.
Greater emphasis on recovery with more rest days.
plan_b_advantages: Includes dedicated hill training to build strength and power.
Hill sessions provide a more intense stimulus than the easy runs in Plan A.
reasoning: For a trail runner aiming to become faster, Plan A is the superior choice. It prioritizes consistent, low-intensity easy runs with specific focus points (rhythm, breathing, cadence), which are crucial for building a solid aerobic base and improving running efficiency – key components of speed. Plan B, while including hill work, is overly reliant on threshold efforts and doesn't provide enough recovery or varied training stimuli. The consistent easy runs in Plan A allow for better adaptation and prevent overtraining, which is vital for a runner looking to improve their pace.
